title: DataJunction as Netflix’s answer to the missing piece of the modern data stack
note: An open-source metric layer sitting between the warehouse and both the dashboards and the experimentation platform, so an experiment metric and the same metric on a dashboard resolve to one definition instead of drifting apart. Worth comparing against how the gold layer and the experiment metrics are defined today, and it is installable rather than an internal-only system.

title: The Lifecycle of LLM-as-a-Judge: Building, Aligning, and Monitoring at scale
note: Treats a judge as a model with a lifecycle: align it to human ratings before trusting it, then keep monitoring that agreement, because a judge shipped once silently drifts away from what the raters meant. The directly usable part is the discipline of measuring judge-to-human agreement as an ongoing metric for any documentation or triage agent scored by an LLM.

title: Measuring the Impact of Personalized Recommendations
note: Frames the value of a personalization system as a measurement problem in its own right - what it adds over a non-personalized baseline - rather than something read off the online metrics of individual model changes. The same framing applies when asked what a production forecast or a curated model is worth, where incremental tests on single changes never add up to the system-level number.

title: Autoscience: How we built agent-driven ML exploration at Faire
note: An agent runs the whole propose-train-score-keep-or-revert loop, so the number of modeling ideas tried stops being bounded by how much engineer attention is free to review each one. The precondition worth noting is that the accept/reject criterion has to be automated and trusted before the loop is worth anything, which is the same gate to clear before letting an agent iterate on forecast specifications.

title: Faire’s agentic development culture
note: Faire's stance is to build the agent harness in-house rather than wait for vendors, on the premise that the harness is what converts raw model capability into reliability. A useful frame for deciding which parts of a data-agent setup are worth owning and which are safe to buy.

title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
note: Skip the version control internals; the liftable pattern is the "superfan" - a per-component agent with access to telemetry and logs, parked in its own Slack channel, which catches subtle anomalies that threshold alerts miss. Also a candid account of the review shift: engineers now check a change's intent rather than every line, and much of the job becomes telling the agent no when it violates a constraint to satisfy a pattern.

title: CASTLE: training natural language search before the first real query
note: Relevance labels come out correct by construction - booked-over-viewed pairs decide positive and negative, and the LLM only writes the query - which keeps LLM-as-judge error out of the training set entirely. They also check the synthetic query distribution against real queries with KL divergence rather than assuming realism, both worth copying when building a golden set for an analytics assistant that has no query history yet.

title: How we built a personal data scientist for every Notion employee
note: An internal analytics assistant grounded in governed Snowflake tables plus the company's own written context, rather than in the warehouse alone. The pairing is the transferable part: a data agent needs the curated layer and the docs that define it, or it answers confidently from tables nobody agreed on.

title: How Notion built a Custom Agent workflow to keep Academy content current
note: An agent spots content gaps, drafts the fix, and only approved drafts get written back to the live platform. That propose-then-approve shape is the one to copy for keeping data model documentation current: the agent does the detection and drafting, a human gate stands between it and anything that ships.

title: Metrics Board: Building an Agent-ready Metrics Layer
note: Metric quality and ownership are enforced when a metric is created rather than audited later, which is the thing that makes the same definitions safe for an agent to query instead of letting it loose on raw tables. Worth reading as a design for your own metric layer: the intake checks and the producer-ownership model are the transferable parts, not the petabyte scale.

title: ShopGym: Realistic, reproducible sandboxes for shopping agents
note: A generated store plus generated tasks gives every agent run the same fixed environment, so a change to the agent can be measured rather than demoed. The same shape applies to your data agents: a frozen snapshot of the warehouse and a generated question set turn text-to-SQL or triage evaluation into a repeatable regression test.

title: A problem well-defined is half solved: Measuring Hypothesis Quality at Booking.com
note: Booking makes the hypothesis itself the quality gate: the evidence behind the idea, the user response expected, and the decision criteria all written down before launch, then scored. That is a rubric you can drop into your own experiment intake so a clear result arrives already attached to a decision instead of a debate.

title: Why Spotify Is Not Using Bayesian A/B Testing
note: A team that runs experimentation at scale explaining why it stayed frequentist and what the Bayesian label does and does not actually change. Read it before your team spends a quarter evaluating a switch, and keep it for the next time someone asks why you haven't.

title: When Can LLMs Replace Humans in A/B Tests?
note: The useful part is the framing: LLM-predicted outcomes substitute for human ones only under assumptions you have to state and defend, not as a free measurement upgrade. Directly relevant if you are tempted to let a judge model stand in for a real metric in a test.

title: From weeks to a day: how we made LLM evaluation fast enough to iterate on
note: Airbnb's cut from weeks to a day came from ordinary engineering on the eval harness - caching, determinism, handling judges that disagree with themselves - not from better models. The layered breakdown is a good checklist for why your own agent evals are too slow to iterate on.

title: Blueberry: Force Multiplier For The On-Call Engineer
note: A Slack-native reasoning harness aimed at the worst minutes of an incident, when nobody yet agrees what is broken, and at turning tribal knowledge into context the agent can reuse. Close to the operational triage work you are building, and concrete about where the harness boundary sits.

title: The Causality Gap: Measuring the True Impact of Voluntary Adoption in Digital Marketplaces
note: For opt-in features, a flat A/B topline can hide a strong product behind low adoption. Randomized encouragement plus DoubleML separates the effect on adopters (ATT) from the rollout effect (ITT), and the gap tells you whether to fix the product or the adoption funnel.

title: Scaling Experimentation Quality at Booking.com
note: A three-pillar quality metric (design, execution, decision) tracked per experiment, plus the finding that strong tool defaults beat enforcement. Useful template for how a working group measures and raises experiment quality.

title: Outlier Handling at Scale in Experimentation
note: Use A/A permutation tests to detect metrics that heavy tails are breaking, then winsorize. Includes a practical heuristic for picking the cap and a max-to-99.9th-percentile ratio as a quick warning sign.

title: A Recap of the 2026 Experimentation Conference at Booking.com
note: Two ideas worth taking: Deliveroo builds its testing standards into the tooling (locked primary metrics, mandatory guardrails), and Booking's micro-conversions cut runtime from 34 to 14 days while keeping the business metric as a guardrail.

title: How we knew COVID was over (and what our models had to unlearn)
note: A decision rule for drifting forecasts: refit, respecify, or hold. Misses that stay one-sided point to a structural problem a refit can't fix. Directly applicable to running a demand forecast in production.

title: Predicting Rider Conversion in Sparse Data Environments with Bayesian Trees
note: A hierarchy of small models where each child is pulled toward its parent's parameters when it has little data. The same pattern fits forecasting down to thin segments without overfitting.

title: Metric Semantic Layer: How Lyft Governs and Scales Key Data Definitions
note: Metric definitions as YAML plus Jinja SQL, admitted only with two or more real use cases, each owned by a business team and a data team. The MCP layer on top lets AI tools answer from the same governed definitions. Maps onto the gold layer and Sigma.

title: Modeling Device Capabilities for Analytics
note: A short gold-layer pattern: a cumulative latest-state table paired with a 28-day histogram table for distribution questions.

title: Partition Finalization in Pinterest's Next-Generation DB Ingestion Framework
note: Answers 'when is a streaming partition complete enough to read?' with an event-time watermark stored in Iceberg table metadata. A good model for gating downstream gold jobs on streaming sources.

title: Eval-driven development: Lessons from evaluating GenAI at scale
note: A practical eval playbook: read outputs first, build a 50 to 100 example golden set with bad examples, keep 3 to 5 calibrated LLM judges, and evaluate agent trajectories, not only final answers.

title: Beyond the model: Engineering AI infra with scientific judgement
note: Argues the methodology belongs in the harness around the model, so analysis is reproducible and auditable. Close to how an agent workforce for data work should be framed.

title: From Traditional ML to AI Agents: How Booking.com Scales AI Observability With Arize AI
note: Two telemetry paths, OpenTelemetry traces for agents and warehouse logs for classic ML, into one observability platform. Relevant to tracing a job-failure triage agent.

title: AI Agent Evaluation
note: Black-box versus glass-box agent evaluation, with task completion scored by an LLM judge as the headline metric.

title: Building an agentic harness that outlasts the model
note: How to design agent infrastructure so it survives model upgrades rather than being rebuilt around each one.

title: Becoming an AI Team
note: A manager's view of moving to an AI-first operating model: the capacity tipping point and how the manager role shifts toward strategy. Worth sharing with the team.

title: From Day 1 to Production: Building Lyft's Analytics & Rides Intelligence Assistant
note: A natural-language analytics assistant going from Streamlit prototype to production service. Skim it if the data agents need a proper front end.
